0.content: Chuychu was Cusco's daughter and Chasca's adoptive younger sister. As a child she resented how Chasca's fights consumed their parents and cost her friends. Once she blurted out "You're the worst vulture here!" and Chasca fled into the wild. Chuychu then learned the fight had started because other children insulted their family, and that adults had told them not to play with Chuychu in case her sister's "sickness" was contagious. She searched the mountains, found Chasca collapsed with shattered hands, burned her own hands lighting a fire, and brought her "home". As adults they argued constantly, Chuychu nagging Chasca not to rush headlong into danger. Chuychu became an expert in treating Abyssal corruption. In 5.1, during the Abyss invasion, monsters ambushed the sisters on the way to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and Chuychu was contaminated. The Traveler purified her, but too late. Chuychu said she had never understood what Chasca lived with, told her to "spread your wings and fly free", and said she was the sister she was proud of. Then she died.

1.content: Chimpu is the pink-plumed Qucusaur who found the abandoned infant Chasca and raised her as her own, always letting her daughters eat first. Coya is Chimpu's daughter, Chasca's Qucusaur "big sister", who always beat her at hide-and-seek. Chasca understands their calls "about nine times out of ten" through sound and body language. When Chimpu sent Chasca back to humans, Coya protested. Years later Coya asked Chasca to leave the tribe and live wild with her; Chasca hesitated, and Coya flew off feeling betrayed.

2.comment: Chasca: Cusco and the human family
2.content: Cusco agreed to take in an orphan and was handed a child tearing at raw meat: "you didn't say it was an orphaned Qucusaurus!" He saw that her fights had no gain behind them, the mark of the Abyss. When a shaman advised returning her to the forest, he refused: "It's too late now." He and his wife then spent years chasing cures and elders. Chasca credits "Chuychu and her- I mean, our parents" with accepting her and swears to defend their tribe for as long as she lives.

3.content: Allpa, a Flower-Feather elder and Flying Captain, brought the young Chasca into the tribe and later took on her education. At first Chasca only wondered whether beating the Elder would end the lectures. The second time, Chasca asked to learn ("Teach me. Become strong... Abyss... want to defeat"). Allpa handed her a woven scroll, "Peacemaker - the Art of Communication", and told her language is humanity's greatest weapon.

4.comment: Chasca: Vuka and the sixth hero
4.content: Vuka ("Transcension") is the Ancient Name of the Flower-Feather Clan. As Chuychu died, grief tore Abyssal energy out of Chasca in an anguished scream; she reined it back in. The spirit of Menilek, Vuka's bearer in the war five hundred years ago, appeared. He spoke of a life of pain risen above and the epitaph "My life's suffering shall be my epitaph... to remember the pain I endured, and finally, transcended." Chasca repeated the words and became the sixth of Natlan's modern heroes. She then helped Mavuika take up the heroes' strength for the counterattack.

5.comment: Chasca: The voice of the Abyss within
5.content: Chasca survived Abyssal contamination as a child, but part of it stayed. It took the form of a voice that first guided her hunting, then urged her to "Fight. Bite. Destroy" whenever people quarrelled, and grew louder the more conflict surrounded her. A shaman said the Abyss had engraved conflict into her soul and that it would worsen with age. Learning to communicate and rely on others weakened it until she thought it gone.

6.content: Soulsniper: Ritual Staff is Chasca's oversized flying gun with a revolver cylinder and reins, forged by Xilonen. Chasca gave only a vague idea. Xilonen then spent a whole day interrogating her about her flying routine and filled the floor with discarded designs, and Chasca fell asleep first. Xilonen then made her memorise a maintenance manual. On receiving it Chasca recalled a scroll's line, "a bullet has the most power when it has yet to leave the chamber", and named her calling: "from this day forth, we shall be the 'Peacemakers.'"
